name: God's Eye View (example)
swalNote: SWAL 3 rigour adopted voluntarily. Allocated SWAL pending a hazard assessment with a customer ANSP; an advisory public-data tool would probably derive SWAL 4.
independence: Not independent: assessed by the development team with AI assistance.

intake.item: God's Eye View, GitHub main 799ff53 (14 Oct 2026). In-house development; fork of an MIT open-source project.
intake.function: Browser-based situational-awareness demonstrator: live public aircraft, vessels, satellites, quakes, fires, cyclones on a 3D globe, with an automated narrator and an analyst HUD. Advisory only; no ATC or separation function.
intake.hazards: No hazard assessment yet. Candidate hazard: an operator acts on stale or wrong public data shown as current. Mitigation in design: FEED / SIMULATED labelling.
intake.isolation: First-level components: feed proxies, layer engine, Director, intel HUD, Exercise mode. Boundaries enforced by import-direction checks; no formal isolation argument.
intake.composition: Developed: ~7k lines (fork modules). Previously developed: ~65k lines inherited upstream. COTS/OSS: CesiumJS 1.138, satellite.js, egm96-universal, Vite, Node 24. Data: OpenSky, adsb.lol, airplanes.live, adsb.fi, AISStream, CelesTrak, USGS, NASA FIRMS, NOAA, OSM. Tools: Prettier, Node test runner, AI coding assistant.
intake.route: Voluntary. Outside EU 2023/1768–1769 and CASA Part 171/172 unless an ANSP integrates it.
intake.novelty: Novel: AI-assisted development, continuous deployment to cloud hosting, public non-authoritative feeds, planned LLM commentary.
intake.evidence: REQUIREMENTS.md (56), VERIFICATION.md with CI-checked traceability, CONFIGURATION-INDEX.md, SECURITY.md, DATA_SOURCES.md, KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md, 1,086 automated tests, CI gates.
intake.history: Forked 24 Sep 2026; demo deployments on Replit; no in-service monitoring.
intake.surface: Public URL on Replit, no login. Entry points: SPA plus ~15 GET JSON proxy endpoints (aircraft, vessels, places, routes, Overpass, terrain, cyclones, FIRMS, CelesTrak). Server-side secrets: AISSTREAM_API_KEY, Google Places key. Browser-bundled by design: GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, CESIUM_ION_TOKEN. Single Node process (vite preview); no database, no uploads, no user data. Repository public; main unprotected.

stages.ref: Owner approval, Pierre Truter (Digital Dynamics Group), 14 Oct 2026 21:08 AEST

ai.note: ISO 42001 lens added on 2026-10-15, assessed against main at eeadc22.

waves.name: Harden
waves.exit: Every Wave 1 security finding closed except V8; re-audit
waves.fixes: Locks down the front end and the proxies: security headers and a strict script policy, rate limits on paid services, dependency scanning, secret hygiene, structured logs and input rules.
waves.unlocks: A hardened base, so company sign-in can be added in Wave 2 without building on holes.

waves.name: Control access
waves.exit: ASVS Level 2 met; AI policy, AIMS scope and intended use issued; re-audit
waves.fixes: Adds company sign-in and roles (viewer, operator, admin), so only known people reach live data, paid services and Exercise mode. Sets up the AI management system: scope, AI policy, roles, intended use and an AI supplier register.
waves.unlocks: Every user known and every action attributable, so the Wave 3 safety work can be written against real roles and real use.

waves.name: Prove safety
waves.exit: No S1–S2 safety or High AI finding open
waves.fixes: Writes the safety evidence: hazard log, failure modes and their effects, a safety level per failure, the safety plan, requirements and verification, and feed-health monitoring. Assesses AI risks and impacts (wrong or missed announcements, effects on the people shown) and logs what the Director announces.
waves.unlocks: A safety argument with evidence behind it, and AI risks and impacts on record, ready for Wave 4 to review and hand over.

waves.name: Assure and hand over
waves.exit: SWAL 3 claim supported; first AIMS internal audit done; evidence pack issued
waves.fixes: Builds the safety case and safety folder, issues the release evidence pack, and runs the first AI management system internal audit.
waves.unlocks: Only steps that need people remain: validation with operational users, an independent process audit and the AI management review.
